title: Vegan Apple Spice Cupcakes
shortDescription: Moist vegan apple spice cupcakes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake time, topped with a fluffy cream swirl frosting.
description: These cupcakes get their moisture from real apple puree, not oil or eggs. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen to get the crumb soft but not gummy. Warm cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger make it taste like fall in one bite. The vegan cream swirl on top stays light and holds its shape for hours.
ingredients: 1 cup vegan butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix apple puree, both sugars, melted coconut oil, almond milk, and vanilla.
Stir the apple cider vinegar into the wet mix. It will foam slightly.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir just until combined, no dry streaks left.
Divide batter evenly into liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat vegan butter until smooth and pale, about 2 minutes.
Add powdered sugar in two batches, then mix in almond milk and cinnamon until fluffy.
Pipe frosting in a tall swirl once cupcakes are completely cool.
Dust with a pinch of cinnamon before serving.
tips: Use unsweetened apple puree, not sweetened applesauce, or the cake will be too sugary.
Do not overmix the batter. Overmixing makes the crumb tough instead of soft.
Let cupcakes cool all the way before frosting, or the swirl will melt and slide.
Chill the frosting bowl for 10 minutes if your kitchen is warm, it pipes cleaner.

faq.question: Can I use homemade apple puree instead of store bought?
faq.answer: Yes, just cook peeled apples until soft, then blend smooth with no added sugar. Let it cool before adding to the batter.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means too much apple puree or an underbaked center. Measure the puree carefully and test with a toothpick before pulling them out.

faq.question: Can I make these gluten free?
faq.answer: Swap the flour for a 1 to 1 gluten free baking blend. I tested this substitution and the crumb stays moist and holds together well.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store them in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or in the fridge for up to 5 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

conclusion: These vegan apple spice cupcakes prove you do not need eggs or dairy for a moist, tender crumb. The apple puree does all the work, and the cream swirl on top makes them feel special enough for any fall gathering.
